full_judgment:
7. As against the aforesaid judgment and decree of reversal dated 14.7.1992 passed in Title Appeal No. 144 of 1991, the Plaintiffs as petitioners obtained the instant rule. 

 8. Mr. Golam Arshed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the impugned judgment and decree as passed by the appellate court below is not a proper judgment of reversal in that it is violative of the mandatory provision of Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In elaborating his submission the learned Advocate submits further that the trial Court upon consideration of the evidence and materials on record arrived at a positive finding to the effect that the plaintiffs have been able to established their right, title and possession in the suit land but the appellate court reversed the decision of the trial court without adverting to the aforesaid finding arrived at by the trial court rather affirmed those findings in his judgment. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits further that the appellate court below allowed the appeal upon reversing the decision of the trial court merely on the point of limitation erroneously holding that the suit is barred by limitation. In substantiating his submission the learned Advocate referred to the finding of the appellate court below to the effect that the previous suit namely title Suit No. 106 of 1968 was withdrawn on 27.3.1969 with a permission to sue afresh on the same cause of action with a condition to pay Rupees 50 to the credit of the contesting defendant, but the instant suit being Title Suit No. 21 of 1985 had been instituted on 3.8.1985 long after an interval of about 16 (sixteen) years as such the suit was, according to the Appellate Court, barred by limitation. Mr. Golam Arshed, the learned Advocate submits that the instant suit being Title Suit No. 81 of 1985 is neither filed on the same cause of action nor the relief claimed in the earlier suit is the same as that of the present one. According to the learned Advocate the previous suit was filed on a different cause of action accrued at that relevant time while the present suit has been filed with the cause of action accrued on 13.5.1985 on which date the defendants threatened to invade the right of the plaintiffs over the suit land. The learned Advocate submits further that in the previous suit the relief claimed was that of correction of record of right and declaration of title while in the present suit the plaintiffs have simply prayed for declaration of their title in the suit land and no prayer for correction of record of right has been made. Therefore, the learned Advocate submits that the subject matter in the previous suit with that the present suit is not the same and in substantiating his submission the learned Advocate refers to the decision of Bhagavan Das Mohesri Vs. Prosannan Dev Raiket and others reported in AIR 1934 Calcutta 433. Wherein a Division Bench of Calcutta High Court relying on AIR 1917 Born 10 and 431. C 752 followed the decision to the effect. 

 12. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and decree of reversal dated 14.7.1992 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, now Joint District Judge in Title Appeal No. 144 of 1991 is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree dated 24.9.1991 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Galachipa in Title Suit No. 81 of Title Suit No. 81 of 1985 is hereby upheld.
